  • Standardize ROCM_ATTN on the blocks-first, content-packed KV cache layout and preserve HND, NHD, and cross-layer stride variants.
  • Enable ROCM_ATTN for KV connectors and expose packed K/V views to NIXL and simple KV offload.
  • Add native HIP paged-decode support for attention sinks and sliding windows.
  • Route short-context decode and large-batch long-context decode to native paged attention; use Triton split-KV for long-context small batches.
  • Keep softcap decode on the unified Triton path because native softcap integration is not yet numerically correct.
  • Keep encoder-decoder cross-attention off ROCM_ATTN; its prefill kernel assumes self-attention cache ownership.
  • Add focused ROCm sink/window, packed-layout, selector, connector, and GPT-OSS evaluation coverage.
  • Merge current upstream main while preserving both upstream packed-layout behavior and the ROCm connector/backend changes.

[ROCm] Enable ROCm Attention Sinks and Connector-Friendly KV Layouts
b4c36ac 
Content-packed KV cache layout for ROCM_ATTN
([num_blocks, num_kv_heads, block_size, 2 * head_size]), enabling
attention sinks (gpt-oss) and connector-friendly blocks-first layouts,
together with the decode/prefill dispatch and kernel fixes it needs:

- Decode dispatch: route long-context decode to the unified Triton
  split-KV (flash-decoding) kernel and keep the native ROCm paged
  attention kernel for short context (crossover at 2048).
- Split-KV segmentation: derive both the 2D/3D threshold and the segment
  count from a single launch-grid occupancy target and the per-rank
  KV-head count, with no per-model tuning.
- prefix_prefill: shrink BLOCK_M for large head_dim (e.g. gemma global
  layers at head_dim 512) so the LDS tile fits within the MI300 limit.
- rocm_aiter_unified_attn: add an identity KV-cache stride order so the
  unified backend's 5D shape is not paired with the content-packed 4D
  order inherited from RocmAttentionBackend.
- Tests for the decode-segment policy and the AITER stride order.

Signed-off-by: Andreas Karatzas <akaratza@amd.com>

[ROCm] Native gpt-oss/gemma decode on ROCM_ATTN + fix Triton unified …
b23222c 
…decode grid

Extend the native ROCm paged-attention kernel and fix a Triton decode bug so
gpt-oss (sinks + sliding window) and gemma-2 (logit softcap) run on the native
ROCM_ATTN path, and so the Triton unified path is correct at any batch size.

- attention.cu: add attention sinks, sliding-window masking (with a whole-
  partition fast-skip so cost scales with the window) and logit softcapping to
  the native paged-attention decode kernel; thread sinks/sliding_window/
  logits_soft_cap through the op, launchers and bindings.
- rocm_attn.py: route short-context decode with these features to the native
  kernel; pass fp32 sinks and the raw sliding-window width; fix the prefix
  prefill off-by-one (context_attention_fwd wants the raw window W, not W-1);
  accept-and-ignore dual-chunk kwargs so Qwen2.5-1M loads.
- triton_unified_attention.py: fix the decode launch grid. The block-to-seq
  layout places sequence i at block (cu_q[i] // BLOCK_Q + i), so a grid of only
  num_seqs dropped the last (num_seqs-1)//BLOCK_Q sequences for any GQA model,
  leaving their output uninitialised. Use the same bound as prefill, matching
  the sibling diffkv/int4 kernels.
- Tests: native parity for sinks/window/softcap, and a high-batch decode
  regression for the Triton grid fix.

Signed-off-by: Andreas Karatzas <akaratza@amd.com>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

[ROCm] Decode gate: batch-aware native routing + softcap guard
37085c4 
The as-shipped _can_use_native_decode_fast_path sent all large-batch or
long-context decode to Triton unified_attention; at num_seqs >
seq_threshold_3D that runs the 2D single-pass kernel, far slower than the
native paged kernel main used for this regime. Decode-heavy serving
regressed up to -38% (Qwen-14B / Qwen-VL / Llama-70B 1k/8k).

Make the gate batch-aware: short context stays native at any batch; long
context uses the Triton 3D split only when the batch is small enough to use
it (num_seqs <= seq_threshold_3D), otherwise native. Recovers Qwen-14B 1k/8k
+28%, Qwen-VL +25%, Llama-70B +19% vs as-shipped; prefill-heavy configs now
match or beat main. Accuracy held: gpt-oss gsm8k 0.945, Qwen-14B 0.895.

Also guard softcap decode onto the unified path: the native softcap decode
integration is numerically wrong (gemma-2 gsm8k 0.01 vs 0.72 on unified),
even though the softcap kernel parity test passes. This path was already
reachable on low-concurrency gemma serving, so this also closes a latent
correctness bug. Fixing native softcap integration is a follow-up.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
